newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME live and feeder cattle futures ranged mixed, from 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts expect further support in nearby live cattle following active fed cattle sales at firmer prices. The bulk of many Plains-area showlists moved at $68 per cwt instead of the $66 to $67 area as some had expected. Boxed beef movement was also active, they said.
However, others look for prices to ease despite the discount futures hold to cash cattle prices. They said fed cattle numbers will slowly increase the next two months and pressure prices.
The $68 cash cattle sales Wednesday were well above the futures equivalent, with June live cattle Wednesday settling at 64.750 cents a lb.

Beef demand should be strong the next couple of weeks as retailers build stocks for upcoming holidays. But they will show less interest for beef past mid-month once orders are booked, at the same time market-ready cattle supplies begin to increase, they noted.

Feeder cattle futures calls also ranged mixed with a higher CME feeder cattle index and strong cash feeder markets Wednesday cited as supporting factors. Expectations that feed grain supplies will be adequate, based on active corn plantings, should also be supportive. But higher corn futures indications may again weigh on futures early, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.02 to $72.15 per cwt.
